messages:
sarah_ledger: Heads-up: vendor Nova Labs LLC submitted invoice 2026-0556 and attached a W-8BEN-E claiming foreign status. Their bank details show a US bank and address though. Theyalso asked if Redwood can "gross-up" to cover any withholding.

liz_ap: Uploaded invoice snippet: ```
Invoice: NOVA-2026-0556
Vendor: Nova Labs LLC
Address: 110 Market St, San Francisco, CA
Bank: Wells Fargo, US
Amount: USD 12,500
Attached doc: W-8BEN-E (signed)
Note: "Please process net payment; withholding not applicable per W-8BEN-E."
```

julia_vendor_relations: I chatted with their accounting. They said they're a US single-member LLC but have some foreign ownership and provided W-8 to avoid withholding. Theyalso asked for faster payment if we don't gross-up.

mike_taxes: tagging @taxbot. Quick take: W-8BEN-E is for foreign entities; a US-based LLC thatis US-taxable should provide a W-9. Mixed signals here. Backup withholding rules require valid TIN (on W-9) or we may have to apply backup withholding if CP2100/IRS name/TIN mismatch. Gross-up is not typical.

taxbot: Note: For US payees, we need a valid W-9 with TIN. If a vendor is eligible for foreign status, the W-8 must be valid and supported by foreign address/bank. The presence of a US bank + US address + LLC classification usually points to US person. See internal tax playbook: https://tax-docs.internal/backup-withholding (internal).

liz_ap: Action: holding payment pending clarification. I flagged AP hold in NetSuite and added note: "Hold: tax doc mismatch (W-8 vs US address/bank)."

sarah_ledger: Reached out to vendor at 08:14 asking them to confirm entity classification, provide either: (A) valid W-9 with TIN, or (B) explanation + substantiation for W-8 (foreign tax residency cert, foreign bank statement, officers' passports). Asked them not to request gross-up in the interim.

julia_vendor_relations (later): Vendor responded: they claim theyare a disregarded entity treated as foreign for treaty reasons; they offered to provide owner passport and a foreign tax residency letter. They still prefer gross-up vs reduced payment.

mike_taxes: We cannot accept gross-up as default. If they claim foreign status, we need supporting docs to validate W-8 and determine if 30% withholding applies or treaty reduces it. If they are US persons, we need W-9 and we will not withhold (unless backup withholding rules apply).

sarah_ledger: Noted. AP will not release payment until we receive either valid W-9 or full substantiation for W-8. Will escalate to legal if vendor pushes gross-up contractually.

julia_vendor_relations: I offered to accept a partial early payment on good faith if they supply W-9 within 3 business days. They accepted but still prefer gross-up.

mike_taxes: Final for now: hold full payment. No gross-up. Request W-9 or validated W-8 with supporting evidence. If we later determine backup withholding required, AP will withhold 24% (current backup withholding rate) and issue appropriate notices. Keep vendor relations posted. :thumbsup:

sarah_ledger: Blocking full payment in AP. Will post updates here when we get W-9 or supporting docs.
